label: A coal miner in South Wales
description: Digs the steam coal that fuels ships around the world.

art.credit: Unknown photographer, The Coal Strike: colliers at Cwmbach, 1910

label: A factory worker in Shenzhen
description: Moves from the countryside to assemble goods for export.

label: A farmhand in the Loire Valley
description: Works land owned by others, far from the Paris salons.

art.credit: Jules Breton, The Song of the Lark, 1884

fr.label: Un ouvrier agricole du Val de Loire
fr.description: Travaille la terre des autres, loin des salons parisiens.

label: A fisherman on the Seto Inland Sea
description: Fishes waters where sea lords and pirates control the routes.

art.credit: Sesshū Tōyō, Dialogue between a Fisherman and a Woodcutter, Muromachi period

label: A Jōmon fisher and gatherer
description: Fishes, gathers and makes the cord-marked pottery that gives the period its name.

art.credit: Bone harpoon head, Jōmon period (Metropolitan Museum of Art)

label: A legionary on Hadrian's Wall
description: Guards the northern frontier of Roman Britain.

label: A merchant's apprentice in Osaka
description: Works for a rice or cloth merchant in the city called the nation's kitchen.

art.credit: Niwa Tōkei, Karamonoya (an imported-goods shop in Osaka), from Settsu meisho zue, 1796-98

label: A mill girl in Lancashire
description: Works long shifts at a cotton mill.

art.credit: Eyre Crowe, The Dinner Hour, Wigan, 1874

label: A peasant in the Hundred Years' War
description: Lives through decades of war, raids and the Black Death.

label: A potter in Roman Gaul
description: Turns red-gloss tableware for markets across the Roman Empire.

art.credit: Gallo-Roman terra sigillata bowl with plant decoration (Musée Lugdunum, Lyon)

label: A rice farmer in a Yayoi village
description: Plants wet rice, newly arrived from the continent, and works bronze and iron.

art.credit: Wooden mortar for pounding rice, Yayoi period, 2nd century BC to 3rd century AD (Tokyo National Museum)

label: A rice farmer in Edo Japan
description: Pays a large share of the harvest in rice tax to the local lord.

art.credit: Utagawa Hiroshige, Kakegawa, from the Reisho Tōkaidō, c. 1847-52

label: A rice farmer in Heian Japan
description: Grows rice and pays tax in kind, far from the court at Heian-kyō.

art.credit: Unknown artist, Rice bales returning to the rich man, Shigisan engi emaki, 12th century

label: A salaryman in Tokyo
description: Commutes into Tokyo for long days at one company, often for a whole career.

label: A serf on a French manor
description: Owes the lord labour on his land and a share of every harvest.

art.credit: Unknown illuminator, Cleric, Knight and Workman, Li Livres dou Santé, late 13th century

label: A servant at Versailles
description: One of thousands of servants who keep the court running.

art.credit: Jean-François de Troy, The Oyster Lunch, 1735

label: A silk weaver in Chang'an
description: Weaves silk for markets that reach Central Asia along the Silk Road.

art.credit: Attributed to Liang Kai, Weaving the Silk, from Sericulture (The Process of Making Silk), 13th century

label: A silk weaver in Lyon
description: Works a Jacquard loom at home. The weavers, the canuts, revolt in 1831 and 1834.

art.credit: Michel-Marie Carquillat (weaver) after Claude Bonnefond, The Duc d'Aumale visiting Carquillat's workshop at the Croix-Rousse, 1844

label: A stonemason at Chartres
description: Cuts and sets stone for the cathedral rebuilt after the fire of 1194.

label: A tea merchant in Hangzhou
description: Trades tea in the Southern Song capital, one of the largest cities in the world.

art.credit: Unknown artist, Tea Contest (Dou jiang tu), Southern Song (Heilongjiang Provincial Museum)

label: A washerwoman on the Seine
description: Washes the laundry of Paris on boats moored along the river.

art.credit: Jean-François Raffaëlli, Two Washerwomen Crossing a Small Park in Paris, 1890

fr.label: Une lavandière sur la Seine
fr.description: Lave le linge de Paris sur des bateaux amarrés le long du fleuve.

label: A worker at Renault's Billancourt plant
description: Builds cars at the huge factory on the Seine, west of Paris.

art.credit: Agence Meurisse, Strikers at the Renault works, Billancourt, 1936

label: A worker at the Tomioka silk mill
description: Reels silk at Japan's first modern silk mill, opened by the government in 1872.

art.credit: Ichiyōsai (Utagawa) Kuniteru II, Silk-reeling at the Tomioka Mill in Kōzuke, c. 1872
